title: 1956 AHSME Problem 43
statement: The number of scalene triangles having all sides of integral lengths, and perimeter less than \(13\) is:

solutions.text:
Write the distinct integer sides in increasing order. Checking the small possibilities under the triangle inequality and perimeter bound gives \[ \begin{aligned} &(2,3,4),\ (2,4,5),\\ &(3,4,5). \end{aligned} \] For \(c\ge6,\) the smallest new scalene candidate satisfying \(a+b\gt c\) is \((3,4,6),\) whose perimeter is already \(13,\) and larger choices cannot qualify. Thus there are \(3\) triangles.

The correct answer is C.
hints: Order the distinct integer sides as \(a\lt b\lt c\) and use \(a+b\gt c\)
List possibilities by the largest side; the perimeter bound leaves only small values of \(c\)
